title: Śākyamuni Buddha (Gautama)
subtitle: A source figure of Buddhist teaching, monastic memory and transregional transmission
timeLabel: Traditional and scholarly dates contested; broad fifth-century BCE navigation range
shortSummary: Śākyamuni is a central gateway into Buddhist thought and pilgrimage geography, but fragmentary early-text biographies, later Buddha legends and sacred narratives must remain layered.
curatorialDescription: The museum connects the historical question, transmitted accounts in early Buddhist texts, the teaching memory of Sarnath and later scriptural representations of the Buddha without projecting a complete later biography into the same period.

Sarnath becomes a full person–event–place–speech–later pilgrimage sample: the real map shows the archaeological site, while sacred meaning and Buddhist memory remain marked as traditional and later layers.
researchNote: Early Buddhist texts do not provide one coherent modern biography. Dates use a broad navigational range; the Sarnath connection is separated into early transmission, heritage memory and later pilgrimage layers.
